Series::retain_grad¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::retain_grad() const -> Series
Series::retain_grad(bool keep) const -> Series

What It Does¶

retain_grad() tells the reverse-mode system to keep stored sensitivity on this Series after a later reverse pass.

This matters most for intermediate results.

By default, non-root intermediate values may participate in propagation during reverse without keeping their own stored public sensitivity afterward. retain_grad() changes that policy for the chosen node so you can inspect the intermediate’s own sensitivity after reverse finishes.

Overload Map¶

  • retain_grad() Shorthand for enabling retention.

  • retain_grad(bool keep) Explicitly set whether retention should be on or off.

Parameters¶

keep (bool)

Whether to keep this series’ sensitivity after reverse-mode runs.

  • true: keep stored sensitivity on this value

  • false: do not keep it

The zero-argument form means keep = true.

Returns¶

Series The current Series value.

This lets the method sit naturally in value-oriented call chains even though its real job is to mutate reverse-mode retention state.

Mathematical Meaning¶

Suppose the forward computation has an intermediate mid and a final scalar objective L.

During reverse-mode, Pluss may need the quantity

dL/dmid

in order to continue propagating back to earlier values.

Without retention, that intermediate sensitivity can be used internally during the reverse pass and then discarded afterward.

With retain_grad(), that same quantity is kept as a readable public result on mid, so mid.sensitivity() becomes meaningful after the pass completes.

This means retain_grad() does not change the mathematics of the derivative. It changes whether a non-leaf keeps its own derivative result for inspection.

When It Matters¶

retain_grad() is mainly for inspection of non-leaf values:

  • branch outputs

  • intermediate transforms

  • staging values in long computational chains

  • any other interior node whose sensitivity you want to inspect after reverse

Without retention, leaf sensitivities are still computed normally. What changes is whether the intermediate keeps its own stored sensitivity around for you to read.

Examples¶

Example 1. Retaining an intermediate keeps its sensitivity available after the reverse pass.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}, pluss::cfg::tracks_slope());

auto mid = x.mul(2.0);
mid.retain_grad();
mid.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "retains=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "mid_has_dL_dmid=" << (mid.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "mid_dL_dmid=" << mid.sensitivity() << "\n";
std::cout << "x_dL_dx=" << x.sensitivity() << "\n";

Here

mid = 2x
L = sum(mid)

So the reverse pass sees

dL/dmid = [1, 1, 1]

because sum contributes one unit of upstream sensitivity to each entry, and

dL/dx = dL/dmid * dmid/dx = [1, 1, 1] * 2 = [2, 2, 2]

because each entry of mid is 2 * x.

Output¶

retains=true
mid_has_dL_dmid=true
mid_dL_dmid=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1, 1]
x_dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 2, 2]

Example 2. Without retention, the intermediate still helps propagate, but it does not keep its own stored sensitivity afterward.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto mid = x.mul(2.0);
mid.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "mid_retains=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "mid_has_dL_dmid=" << (mid.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "x_has_dL_dx=" << (x.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

The chain rule still reaches the leaf, so x keeps its stored sensitivity. What is missing is only the intermediate’s own retained public result.

Output¶

mid_retains=false
mid_has_dL_dmid=false
x_has_dL_dx=true

Example 3. The boolean overload can turn retention back off.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto mid = x.mul(4.0);
mid.retain_grad(false);
mid.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "retains=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "mid_has_dL_dmid=" << (mid.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

retains=false
mid_has_dL_dmid=false

Example 4. The state change itself is visible immediately through retains_grad(), even before any reverse pass happens.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
auto mid = x.mul(3.0);

std::cout << "before=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
mid.retain_grad();
std::cout << "after=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

before=false
after=true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • retain_grad() does not run reverse-mode by itself. It only changes what is kept after a later reverse pass.

  • This method does not change dL/dx on earlier tracked leaves. It only changes whether an intermediate keeps its own dL/dmid.

  • The public return type is Series, but the real effect is retention-state mutation on the receiver.

Summary¶

Use retain_grad() when an intermediate Series should keep its own stored sensitivity after reverse so you can inspect it later.

See Also¶

  • Series::retains_grad: inspect the keep-state flag.

  • Series::sensitivity: read the stored sensitivity after reverse.

  • Series::reverse: run the reverse pass that populates the stored values.
